pr.title: Relay through a repository agent.relay names, and let agents message each other across repositories
pr.head: e2197dca51eaf2960d99b968112f5efaf1456ef6

summary: The relay carries encrypted agent registrations and messages between your machines through hidden Git refs. It currently uses the repository each session works in, which prevents sessions in different repositories from finding each other.

This layer adds agent.relay, so a team directory or your own configuration can select one shared relay repository. Sessions retain their work repository for display and privacy notices while the daemon groups transport work by the selected location.
The next layer shares the repository inbox by location. This layer keeps peer inbox sends in their existing work repository and refuses them when the registered relay location differs.

cards.title: Terms used here
cards.html:
• Work repository: the GitHub repository the session works in.
  • Relay location: the repository that holds encrypted presence and message refs.
  • Presence: a registration with an expiry time, so other machines can find the session.
  • Outbox: local ref updates waiting for the daemon to push.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: One P2 finding remains open: moving the last local session off a shared relay strands the deletion of its old presence. The exact-head gate passed, and 230 focused relay, agent, configuration, and permission tests passed. A temporary local reproduction confirmed the cleanup failure.

groups.title: Choose and approve a location
groups.kicker: The destination setting follows the existing configuration trust boundary.
intro: A relay location is either origin, the current work repository, or github:owner/repo. Making agent.relay a destination means a committed configuration value is read from the default branch and requires the person to allow it before records leave the machine.

checks.text: Traced the new setting through Config.setting, default-branch configuration loading, NotAllowed handling, and the registration admission path; the focused configuration and relay tests passed.

files.note: Adds the destination setting and validates its supported value forms.
Exercises accepted and refused setting forms through the CLI.

groups.title: Run one job per relay location
groups.kicker: The daemon separates where records travel from where the session works.
intro: A relay job now serves every local session that selects the same location. It prefers a checkout of that location and otherwise creates a bare Git repository under local state, so the work repository receives no shared-relay refs.

Configured locations must be private or internal and writable. Bare-repository commands use GitHub CLI credentials, fetch only relay refs, and preserve global Git hooks. The location cache deliberately retains its last successful privacy and permission answer when a later API lookup fails.

checks.text: Origin-only relays retain their existing behavior when no checkout remains. Shared-relay cleanup must still work after registrations stop choosing an external location.

files.note: Groups transport, caches, remote sessions, and review targets by location while preserving each presence’s work repository.

checks.text: Moving the last local session to origin removes its old registration before cleanup runs. The old job no longer takes the bare-clone branch, leaves its presence deletion queued forever, and advertises an unreachable session until its lease expires. Reproduced with temporary relay fixtures; retain location history or reuse the existing shared bare clone for cleanup.

files.note: Covers shared transport, destination approval, location refusal, credentials, hooks, originless checkouts, and legacy records.

groups.title: Keep each message’s source
groups.kicker: Registrations carry their location, and messages carry their work repository.
intro: An agent registration records both its work repository and the location used to relay it. A registration that awaits approval remains local until the daemon sees the approval.

A message that crosses work repositories names its source. If that source is private, internal, or unknown, the event line and read output warn the receiving agent to keep private details out of anything it writes in the other repository. Messages queued by older versions with neither source field retain their previous delivery behavior.

checks.text: Focused tests passed for private-to-public and private-to-private notices, record validation, originless senders, and legacy delivery; traced the record’s source fields through both local and relayed delivery.

files.note: Resolves registration locations, admits approved sessions, preserves message source metadata, and renders crossing notices.
Checks the notice seen by each reader and validates complete and legacy source records.

groups.title: Expose the relay state
groups.kicker: CLI output reports the location and explains waiting or refused transport.
intro: The new project agent relay show command explains the directory’s effective location, the configuration that selected it, and the last transport result. Existing agent and watch output now includes waiting approval, location visibility, write permission, and bare-clone use.
Peer inbox transport remains deferred in this layer. Its send path rejects registrations that use another repository as the relay location.

checks.text: The focused permission tests passed for project agent relay show; traced agent read JSON and text output and the existing watch status adapter.

files.note: Adds location inspection, source notices, status reporting, and the temporary inbox guard.
Allows the read-only relay inspection command in Codex rules.
Verifies command permission behavior through the generated host rules.

groups.title: Document configuration and crossings
groups.kicker: User and agent guidance explain the transport boundary and private sources.
intro: The command guide explains where to put agent.relay, how the person allows committed destinations, and why external locations must be private or internal. The message skill tells agents to preserve source confidentiality and leave destination approval to the person.
The shared-relay plan moves to in-progress and records this layer’s decisions in section 8. The repository inbox and the real two-machine acceptance run remain for later work.

checks.text: Section 8 explicitly chooses last-known privacy and permission on a failed location lookup and limits new bare clones to configured locations. The cleanup finding concerns completing queued deletion after a previously configured location is left.

files.note: Documents relay settings, approval, transport state, and message crossing notices.
Updates agent routing guidance and the private-source handling rules.
Records the two-layer rollout and implementation decisions in section 8.
